title: Rob Walling's B2B content strategy: map content to the five stages of customer awareness
summary: Rob explains how to prioritize B2B SaaS content using the five stages of customer awareness (unaware, problem, solution, product, most aware). He covers three ways to place a prospect in a stage and gives SaaS examples per stage, advising founders to start at the bottom of the funnel and work upward.

principles.text: Prioritize content with an awareness framework; generic top-of-funnel posts without a plan flopped for him.
principles.quote: the reason it did not work in retrospect is because I didn't have any type of plan or strategy or framework work to how to prioritize what content should we do

principles.text: Start content at the bottom of the funnel (most aware) and work backwards; it helps both sales and marketing.
principles.quote: if you have nothing if you have none of this I would start at that most aware stage creating the content examples I give there and I would work my way backwards

principles.text: Find a prospect's stage by asking on sales calls about purchase timing and which competitors they're comparing.
principles.quote: you should ask on your sales calls when do you plan to make a purchase are you comparing us to other products which other products this will tell you a lot

principles.text: The unaware stage is the hardest in B2B; don't spend much effort there.
principles.quote: we won't spend a ton of time on it on on unaware because in B2B you really kind of don't want to be there

principles.text: Versus, alternative-to and case study content closes deals even for outbound-only sales teams with no content marketing.
principles.quote: even if you are only doing outbound sales and you're only talking to prospects one-on-one you're not doing any content marketing these things start to become valuable to help you close a sale

principles.text: Late-stage buyers need features, not just benefits: deep docs, long demos and compliance content.
principles.quote: this is where you have to break the Paradigm you have to get into features and not just talk about benefits
